issues.label: Failure to comply mandatory consecutive sentence
issues.why: R.C. 2921.331(D) requires the failure-to-comply sentence to run consecutively to any other prison term, potentially conflicting with concurrent ordering.

issues.label: Firearm specification for dangerous ordnance count
issues.why: The court must confirm the six-year firearm specification was properly attached and lawfully imposed under R.C. 2941.145/2929.14.

issues.label: Multiple firearm specifications and R.C. 2929.14(B)(1)(g)
issues.why: Whether more than one firearm specification could or should have been imposed given multiple qualifying offenses.

issues.label: Allied offenses of similar import merger
issues.why: Involuntary manslaughter, aggravated vehicular homicide, and vehicular assault may merge under R.C. 2941.25 as arising from the same conduct.

issues.label: Two involuntary manslaughter counts merger
issues.why: Both manslaughter counts stem from one death and may constitute allied offenses requiring merger.

issues.label: Receiving stolen property double counting
issues.why: Receiving stolen property appears in both cases and as an underlying felony, raising merger and duplicative punishment concerns.

issues.label: Consecutive sentence R.C. 2929.14(C)(4) findings
issues.why: The court must make and incorporate statutory findings to lawfully impose consecutive sentences.

issues.label: Sentences within statutory ranges
issues.why: Each imposed term must fall within the authorized range for its offense degree.

issues.label: Offense degree and felony classification accuracy
issues.why: Correct felony levels determine permissible sentencing ranges and mandatory terms.

issues.label: Mandatory vs. discretionary prison terms
issues.why: Certain offenses (e.g., aggravated vehicular homicide, firearm specs) carry mandatory time affecting lawful imposition.

issues.label: Reagan Tokes indefinite sentencing applicability
issues.why: Qualifying first/second-degree felonies may require indefinite sentences under S.B. 201.

issues.label: Postrelease control notification
issues.why: Failure to properly impose and notify PRC renders a sentence contrary to law.

issues.label: R.C. 2929.11 and 2929.12 consideration
issues.why: Court must consider sentencing purposes and seriousness/recidivism factors.

issues.label: Eighth Amendment proportionality/cruel-and-unusual challenge
issues.why: Hampton raises whether the aggregate sentence is disproportionate or cruel and unusual.

issues.label: Due process and fair sentencing
issues.why: Fifth and Fourteenth Amendment claims require the sentence comport with due process.

issues.label: Article I Sections 9 and 16 Ohio guarantees
issues.why: State constitutional excessive-punishment and due-process protections must be analyzed.

issues.label: Validity of guilty plea (Crim.R. 11)
issues.why: A knowing, intelligent, voluntary plea underlies the convictions being sentenced.

issues.label: Standard of review for sentencing appeal
issues.why: R.C. 2953.08(G)(2) governs whether the appellate court may modify or vacate.

issues.label: Aggregate sentence arithmetic accuracy
issues.why: The stated totals must correctly reflect the individual and consecutive/concurrent terms.

issues.label: Forfeiture specification disposition
issues.why: The court must properly order forfeiture of the dangerous ordnance under the specification.

issues.label: Jail-time credit calculation
issues.why: Proper credit for presentence confinement must be determined and awarded.
